## Discovery & Translational Science

* **Age-dependent cardiovascular response to postmenopausal estrogen therapy** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.06.29.734522)
  * Preclinical evaluation in `Ldlr⁻/⁻` mice following ovariectomy demonstrated that 17β-estradiol (E2) therapy failed to reduce established atherosclerosis in aging mice (14 months), elevating circulating IFNγ, impairing HDL cholesterol efflux/antioxidant function, and increasing hepatic 4-HNE via altered estrogen receptor expression (decreased ERα, increased GPER).
  * In contrast, E2 administration in young mice (9 months) attenuated systemic and plaque inflammation while promoting atherosclerosis regression.
  * Suppressing inflammation via `Ifng⁻/⁻` bone marrow transplantation restored HDL function and enabled E2-mediated plaque reduction in aging mice.

* **Cardiomyocyte Perm1 identified as essential regulator of cardiac bioenergetic reserve** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.03.753324)
  * Constitutive and adult-induced `αMHC` knockout mouse models revealed that loss of the PGC-1/ERR-regulated protein Perm1 reduced complex I- and complex I+II-supported mitochondrial respiration by 20–25% without altering overall mitochondrial density or resting cardiac structure/function through 12 months.
  * Perm1 deletion selectively reduced MICOS complex components IMMT (MIC60) and CHCHD3 (MIC19) and shifted mitochondrial sub-populations away from subsarcolemmal sites.
  * Perm1-deficient mice exhibited lower treadmill exercise capacity and failed to maintain cardiac ATP levels under submaximal workload, demonstrating a cardiomyocyte-intrinsic requirement for bioenergetic expansion during stress.

* **Hepatic constitutive androstane receptor confers sex-specific protection against MASLD** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.08.757558)
  * Western diet studies in `Car⁻/⁻` mice showed that loss of Constitutive Androstane Receptor (CAR) accelerated hepatic steatosis, inflammation, fibrosis, and dysregulation of bile acid, cholesterol, and gut microbiota exclusively in male mice.
  * Fecal microbiota transplantation and co-housing experiments demonstrated that a `Car⁺/⁺` microbiota conferred protection against diet-induced liver injury in `Car⁻/⁻` hosts.
  * Transcriptomic profiling across human clinical cohorts confirmed progressive downregulation of hepatic CAR expression in advanced stages of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.

* **U-shaped association of plasma renin activity with MACE informs MRA therapy in hypertension** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.11.26352940)
  * A retrospective cohort study of 16,600 adults with hypertension demonstrated a U-shaped association between baseline plasma renin activity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), with minimum risk observed at 1.17 ng/mL/h and elevated risk at <0.3 ng/mL/h (adjusted HR = 1.29) and >3.0 ng/mL/h (adjusted HR = 1.19).
  * Time-varying Cox analysis indicated that mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) therapy significantly reduced MACE risk in low-renin cohorts (<0.3 ng/mL/h [HR = 0.59] and 0.3–1.0 ng/mL/h [HR = 0.71]), whereas no benefit was observed at high renin levels (>3.0 ng/mL/h [HR = 1.07]).

* **Maternal hyperglycemia induces stage-dependent skeletal muscle remodeling in offspring** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.03.755574)
  * Offspring of streptozotocin-induced hyperglycemic mice displayed persistent reductions in body weight, skeletal muscle mass, and myofiber cross-sectional area at 4 and 8 weeks post-birth.
  * Early post-weaning muscle (4 weeks) exhibited type I/IIA hybrid myofibers and upregulation of myogenic and proliferative genes, whereas 8-week muscle shifted toward downregulation of mitochondrial and oxidative phosphorylation pathways.

* **NuPath biosensor platform enhances GPCR functional screening** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42858819/)
  * Development of NuPath, a higher-sensitivity biosensor derived from the TRUPATH framework, expands detection limits for both basal and agonist-induced G-protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation.

* **Single-cell transcriptomics links HERC5 program to osteosarcoma pulmonary metastasis** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42858644/)
  * Combined bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing identified a HERC5-associated, immune-attenuated transcriptomic profile predictive of pulmonary relapse and metastatic progression in osteosarcoma.

## Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Biotech]** **Liquidia label decision triggers market cap contraction** [BioStocks on X](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2108912208323477974)
  * Unconfirmed social media commentary highlights a $4 billion drop in market capitalization for Liquidia ($LQDA) following regulatory label terms impacting product positioning.

## Public Health & Policy

* **US trust in science leads international peers despite low health system confidence** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/10/10/u-s-trust-science-higher-than-other-nations-wellcome-survey/?)
  * Data from a Wellcome survey indicate higher overall public trust in science in the US relative to international peers, although only 40% of US respondents reported high confidence in domestic hospitals and clinics (comparable to levels in Uruguay and Portugal).

* **Addressing global disparities in essential drug availability** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2609409?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * NEJM perspective highlights systemic regulatory, economic, and supply chain barriers that limit patient access to approved therapeutics across international jurisdictions.

* **Refining measurement of health-related social needs in older populations** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2608580?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * Perspective discusses methodological gaps and mismeasurement issues in evaluating social determinants of health and health-related social needs among older adults.

* **Evaluating inclusion criteria in clinical definitions of infertility** [NEJM](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp2603604?af=R&rss=currentIssue)
  * NEJM commentary examines current diagnostic frameworks for infertility and opportunities to update inclusion standards across clinical settings.

**Worth watching:** Plasma renin activity stratification in hypertension trials to prospective test low-renin patient selection for MRA therapy.

- Pure Science
    - [What if you try to sandwich a cube between two portals?](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/31kyER-8dak) -- minutephysics
        - Extending a piston into a blue portal causes it to exit the connected orange portal and collide with its own back, as portals have no internal space.
        - If the piston is weak, it crumples upon self-collision as if pushing against a solid wall.
        - If the piston is rigid and the portals are fixed or extremely heavy, the piston simply stops expanding.
        - Based on momentum conservation and Newton's third law, if the portals are free to move, the forces from the entering and exiting piston push the portals apart.
